subject: Materials Science
title: Corrosion Inhibitors
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Corrosion Inhibitors.

hook.text: Add a few parts per million of the right chemical to cooling water and corrosion drops 90%.

buildup.text: Corrosion inhibitors are chemicals that adsorb onto metal surfaces, forming a thin protective film.

discovery.text: Anodic inhibitors suppress metal dissolution. Cathodic inhibitors slow the reduction reaction. Mixed do both.

twist.text: Under-dosing an anodic inhibitor can be worse than no inhibitor — it concentrates attack at unprotected spots.

climax.text: Engine coolant contains corrosion inhibitors that protect aluminum, cast iron, copper, and solder simultaneously.

punchline.text: A trace of the right molecule can armor a million square centimeters of metal.

quiz.question: What risk does under-dosing an anodic inhibitor create?
options: Corrosion concentrates at unprotected spots, causing localized attack
The metal surface becomes too smooth
